title: CRL-Minimax: Algorithm Pseudocode
subtitle: High-level pseudocode for the implemented continual-RL algorithms.

sections.text: This collection documents, as faithful high-level pseudocode, the three core algorithms of the CRL-Minimax continual reinforcement-learning system. A single shared-trunk, multi-head GLOBAL policy learns a sequence of tasks (Atari games) while retaining performance on all past tasks. The current method (Part A, config ppo.method = constrained) casts consolidation as a primal-dual min-max saddle: a throwaway LOCAL specialist supplies each task's value floor, and the global policy maximizes the weighted past-task objective subject to a one-sided value constraint. Experts are NOT stored; past-task quantities are re-estimated from fresh, replay-free rollouts. Each doc mirrors the code AS IMPLEMENTED, including its two faithful magnitude-only deviations, not an idealized version.
Source math: docs/Updated_Objective_for_CRL.pdf (Part A, eqs 1-48). This branch implements Part A only; Part B (stored expert models) has been stripped from the code.

03  Shared PPO Update Core.   Source: crl/ppo/trainer.py (PPOTrainer.optimize_batches). The one reusable clipped-PPO optimizer shared by the local and global phases: per-stream actor-coeff times clipped surrogate, standard value MSE, entropy bonus, single global grad-norm clip. Actor coefficients are renormalized by their sum (prevents a large dual coefficient from starving the shared critic). ALL continual-learning weighting enters only through the actor coefficients.

04  Part A: Min-Max Consolidation, experts NOT stored (CURRENT method).   Source: crl/ppo_continual.py (PPOAlternationTrainer), crl/ppo/trainer.py (Local/GlobalTrainer), crl/duals/controllers.py (ProjectedAscentDual). Three-checkpoint cycle piG-minus -> piL -> piG-plus. Stage 1 is plain PPO; stage k>=2 runs a local PPO phase producing the frozen floor V_k^L, then a global primal-dual phase maximizing the weighted past objective under the one-sided squared hinge F_k = [V_k^L - V_k^G]_+^2 <= eps, with current-task coeff 2*mu*[V_k^L - V_k^G]_+ and dual mu <- [mu + eta(F_k - eps)]_+. Replay-free; V are Monte-Carlo; only the actor is constrained. Verification: Part A derivation math-verifier SOUND; implementation code-verifier PASS against eqs 26 / 38 / 40 / 47.

05  Windowed Off-Policy Expert Value-Agreement.   Source: crl/ppo/expert_eval.py, crl/envs/atari.py (make_snapshot_env). A cheap off-policy DIAGNOSTIC of whether a policy matches its task's expert's windowed value from the expert's own states. BUILD (once per task): roll the expert greedily, snapshot ale.cloneState() each step, pick an adaptive horizon, keep consequential windows. EVALUATE (per checkpoint): restore O(1), roll the policy greedily over the equal-length window, report the one-sided shortfall. Reported ALONGSIDE the greedy-100 anchor, never as a standalone forgetting number. Verification: code-verifier PASS against the design doc.

Read 03 first: it is the optimizer that 04's local and global phases both call. Then 04 for the continual-learning control flow, and 05 for the value-agreement diagnostic reported alongside greedy-100. Each PDF pairs its pseudocode with the equation numbers it realizes; the JSON sources under specs/ are the regenerable inputs to render_pseudocode.py.
